items.summary: On Nov 13, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed lower as concerns over Nvidia pressured technology shares. Nvidia's stock fell 2% for its sixth straight week after CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid revelations of extramarital affairs. The Dow rose modestly to 52,347.55 while the S&P 500 lost 30.73 points and the Nasdaq dropped 229.82 points. For the week, however, all three indexes posted gains as Nvidia's decline snapped a four-week losing streak for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq. Separately, October producer prices rose 6.5% year over year, keeping expectations for a December rate hike intact.
items.title: US Tech Shares and Inflation Data Weigh on Markets Amid Nvidia Leadership Uncertainty

items.summary: NVIDIA's cuBLAS, in CUDA Toolkit 13.4.2, accelerates full double-precision (FP64) dense matrix multiplications by breaking numbers into integer pieces and multiplying them exactly on GPU Tensor Cores via the Automatic Dynamic Precision framework. Two new algorithms—Ozaki-II, which needs roughly half the GEMMs of Ozaki-I at FP64 accuracy, and a 2M complex-multiply method—are chosen automatically with no code changes. DGEMM runs up to 5.5x faster on VR NVL72 and 3.9x on GB200; CCSD quantum-chemistry workloads reach 11.5x over native FP64, while BerkeleyGW materials simulations gain 6.6x.
items.title: NVIDIA cuBLAS FP64 Emulation Speeds Double-Precision Matrix Math on Tensor Cores

items.summary: A global Microsoft Outlook and Teams outage eased on Nov 3 after more than 24 hours of disruption, though the company gave no full-recovery timeline. Server issues tied to Exchange Online were blamed, with AI ruled out as a cause. Reports climbed around 5:25pm GMT on Nov 12 (1:25am Nov 13 Singapore time), one of Microsoft's longest-ever disruptions and its second this year after January and October incidents. Downdetector logged over 7.4 million reports, peaking near 20,000 a minute—more than 1,500 times normal levels. The outage affected government agencies from Australia to the US, trading firms, airlines, insurers like Aviva, shipping giant Maersk, and Taiwanese securities firms, some of which resorted to faxing trades or paper records. Analysts warned it deepens concerns over reliance on Big Tech amid steep switching costs.
items.title: Microsoft Outlook and Teams Outage Eases After More Than a Day; Recovery Timeline Uncertain

items.summary: A new research effort claims the most powerful Chinese open-weight AI models were trained on U.S.-banned Nvidia Blackwell GPUs, revealing a major gap in export controls. Will DePue of Unemployment Labs analyzed model weights from DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group, finding fingerprints consistent with Blackwell training; White House adviser Michael Kratsios also cited intelligence sources implicating Moonshot. Epoch AI estimates roughly 2 million chips entered China through hidden-destination schemes in 2024–2025, while about 275,000 Nvidia accelerators went to Malaysia and ~600,000 H200s are stockpiled in Hong Kong. The article notes these models may not have been trained solely on banned chips—offshore data centers remain a plausible route—and questions whether holding back shipments would spur domestic Chinese production.
items.title: Export-banned Nvidia Blackwell chips power China's leading AI models

items.summary: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang stepped down after admitting an affair with Alice Huang, who ran Megaspeed, a major Nvidia chip buyer. The case has spotlighted tensions in Singapore's role as a global semiconductor hub. Last year it was Nvidia's second-largest market globally, yet less than 1% of its earnings came from chips physically present there, since the island routes orders onward to Asia. Since US export restrictions on advanced chips reached China in 2022, officials worry countries like Singapore could be used for illicit access; Megaspeed is suspected of giving Chinese firms backdoor chip access via data centres in Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand. Singapore has charged four companies and five individuals but brought no charges against Megaspeed-linked parties after finding insufficient evidence against Alice Huang.
items.title: How the Jensen Huang scandal created a headache for business-friendly Singapore

items.summary: Microsoft apologized for a global service outage affecting Outlook, Teams, and Microsoft 365 products used by over 430 million people worldwide. The technical issue stemmed from a network capacity upgrade rather than cyber or AI causes. Services were broadly recovering nearly 24 hours after beginning on Thursday at 17:54 GMT, with partial recovery reported by Friday morning and broader improvements across regions. The outage disrupted governments in Japan, the Philippines, India, Singapore, and Australia, plus institutions including hospitals, courts, rail networks, and UK NHS services.
items.title: Microsoft Global Outage Recovery and Impact

items.summary: Jensen Huang has resigned from Nvidia, the AI chipmaker, following reported affairs with an Nvidia executive and a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. His departure has sent shockwaves through the global economy. The fallout remains unresolved as criticism grows over what appears to be a lack of action from US commerce secretary Howard Lutnick.
items.title: Nvidia Scandal Fallout Continues Amid Criticism of US Commerce Secretary's Inaction

items.summary: Nvidia co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang stepped down after 33 years, sending shockwaves through the startup ecosystem. Investors say his departure removes a dominant champion that backed nearly every AI-native company from application to neocloud, injecting tens of billions annually across 105 rounds this year alone as its largest investor in many deals. His conservative successor Colette Kress is expected to write smaller checks and be more selective, threatening valuations and early-stage funding—especially outside the U.S., where Nvidia's support created a gap no one can fill.
items.title: Jensen Huang's Departure Blasts Big Hole in AI Startup Funding

items.summary: A widespread outage shut down Microsoft 365 services for businesses, governments, and tens of millions of users worldwide. Beginning around noon Thursday on the East Coast with Outlook failures tracked by Downdetector, the incident quickly spread to more than 70 countries. Microsoft ruled out a cyberattack or AI involvement, attributing it to an earlier network capacity upgrade following recent changes. As services restore, users may face inbox clutter and notification floods.
items.title: Microsoft 365 Crawls Back After a 24-Hour Outage

items.summary: The Electrek Podcast previews its weekly sustainable transport and energy episode, airing live every Friday at 4 p.m. ET on YouTube with an accompanying site post and embedded stream link. After the show ends around 5 p.m., the video is archived online while audio remains available across podcast apps.
items.title: Podcast: Tesla trims are falling like flies, Hyundai 2027 lineup, and BYD’s Rolls-Royce

items.summary: An analysis by DeKleptocracy found Trump bought $1m–$5m of Nvidia stock as his administration rescinded a rule blocking advanced US AI chips from China in May 2025. Nvidia shares rose after the announcement, and he made further purchases between December 2025 and January 2026 to allow H200 chip sales—six times better than what was available in China at the time.
items.title: Trump's Nvidia Stock Purchases Amid China Export Rule Changes

items.summary: On Friday, a regulatory filing revealed that Soros Fund Management significantly increased its third-quarter stake in Intel, building a 2.83 million-share position valued at $340.3 million from just 100,000 shares held by end of June.
items.title: Soros Fund Management Ramps Up Intel Stake in Q3

items.summary: NPR's Scott Detrow spoke with Dylan Patel of SemiAnalysis about the implications of Jensen Huang leaving Nvidia. The conversation centers on whether his departure creates a genuine opening for Nvidia's competitors in the AI and semiconductor industry, exploring what this leadership change might mean for competitive dynamics.
items.title: Is There an Opening for Nvidia's Competitors After Jensen Huang's Departure?

items.summary: Institutional interest in Anthropic's $64 billion IPO is outpacing SpaceX's earlier roadshow, with the book roughly two times oversubscribed on day one and six times by Thursday. Investors weigh whether Anthropic can sustain its AI lead as rivals like Google catch up and keep premium pricing beyond coding. Valuation hinges on projected 2028 revenue of $270-280 billion; sell-side sees 2026 at $52-53 billion rising to $135-137 billion in 2027, while buy-side estimates run 10-15% higher and one investor sits about 30% below the sell side. Benchmarks include SpaceX (2029 revenue) and CrowdStrike.
items.title: Investor Demand and Valuation Uncertainty in Anthropic's IPO Roadshow

items.summary: Despite co-founding and leading Nvidia for 33 years, Jensen Huang's roughly 870 million shares—about 3.6% of the company—did not grant him absolute control. Nearly 800 million were held via trusts shared with his wife; about 70 million directly. His November 12 resignation underscores that large ownership does not guarantee board authority.
items.title: Jensen Huang's Nvidia Shareholding Fell Short of Board Control

items.summary: This Semafor report details how Nvidia, under co-founder Jensen Huang, leveraged an unprecedented level of influence to shape U.S. chip export controls. Tim Teter, the company's general counsel, relayed President Trump's wishes directly to government officials and congressional staffers, framing objections—like a cloud-customer requirement—as unworkable or politically motivated. Nvidia reportedly claimed technical infeasibility for location-verification provisions later proven false when the technology launched months after being shown privately. The article frames this as an 'intense trust deficit' between Nvidia and Washington, noting that Huang's downfall has shaved $1.5 trillion off market value.
items.title: How Nvidia's Jensen Huang and Trump Jumped Guardrails on Chip Export Controls

items.summary: Bloomberg Opinion commentary by Beth Kowitt argues that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who stepped down Thursday (Nov 12) amid turmoil following revelations of an extramarital relationship with a company vice president, may prove the notion of an irreplaceable founder-CEO to be a myth. The board named CFO Collette Kress as interim CEO but faces planning for a future without Huang at the helm. Unlike Jobs and Bezos, who built companies designed to survive their departure through institutionalized structures and succession plans, Nvidia lacks a chairman, number two or public succession plan, with Huang having 60 direct reports while other executives focused on narrow responsibilities. Khurana notes that Apple's stock returned nearly 2,800 per cent during Cook's tenure versus Amazon's roughly 50 per cent increase under Jassy since 2021.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Stepping Down Raises Questions About Company Succession and Leadership Structure

items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 31.53 points (0.42%) to 7,560.87 while the Nasdaq dropped 230.13 points (0.91%) to 25,135.96; only the Dow rose modestly (+46.14 points). Nvidia's sixth straight weekly decline followed CEO Jensen Huang's resignation amid China-spying allegations and succession uncertainty involving Arm Holdings' Rene Haas. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 3.7%, with Fed officials signaling further rate hikes as inflation remained elevated.
items.title: US Stocks Close Lower on Nvidia Leadership Uncertainty and Rate-Hike Fears

items.summary: A controversy involving Jensen Huang, a businesswoman suspected of spying for China who worked at Singapore-based Megaspeed, has prompted US lawmakers from both parties to push stronger restrictions on China's access to advanced AI chips. Lawmakers seek to close loopholes allowing Chinese firms to rent overseas computing power with restricted Nvidia chips. Proposed rules could add export controls and licensing requirements for shipments to Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Singapore. Southeast Asia's data-centre industry has expanded rapidly—Malaysia approved 385.7 billion ringgit ($94.67 billion) of related investment since 2021—and the AI boom is supporting regional growth. Some analysts expect tighter rules could harm prospects, while others believe expansion will continue.
items.title: Jensen Huang Controversy and Tightening AI Chip Controls in Southeast Asia
